title: The Karvy Stock Broking Scam
dek: A major brokerage allegedly pledged clients' own shares as collateral for its own loans, without their knowledge, affecting tens of thousands of investors before regulators stepped in.

promise.quote: Client securities held by Karvy Stock Broking will be used only as authorised by each client, not pledged for the firm's own borrowing.
promise.context: Karvy is alleged to have transferred client securities to its own demat account and pledged them to raise loans for its real estate arm, without client authorisation.

target.description: Client securities held strictly in clients' own accounts, used only for that client's own transactions, consistent with SEBI custody and margin-pledging rules.
target.standard: SEBI regulations on broker custody of client securities and prohibitions on commingling client and proprietary assets.

reality.description: SEBI barred Karvy Stock Broking from taking on new clients in the securities market in November 2019, citing unauthorised transfer and pledging of client securities affecting roughly 95,000 client accounts and reportedly worth ₹2,300–2,700 crore depending on the source. SEBI later imposed penalties on the firm and its chief executive, and the Enforcement Directorate separately attached assets worth roughly ₹1,984 crore in a related money-laundering probe.

gap.note: Reported figures for the value of misused securities vary between roughly ₹2,300 crore and ₹2,700 crore across sources; this investigation has not reconciled the two.

timeline.detail: SEBI restricts Karvy from taking on new broking clients, citing the securities misuse.

timeline.detail: The Enforcement Directorate attaches roughly ₹1,984 crore in assets in its money-laundering probe.

timeline.label: SEBI penalties imposed
timeline.detail: SEBI fines Karvy and its chief executive; further penalties follow after non-payment.

legalStatus.summary: This is a stub entry. Regulatory penalties and an ED money-laundering attachment have been reported; this investigation has not yet examined whether any individual has faced criminal conviction.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: SEBI's finding of unauthorised use of client securities, and the resulting regulatory penalties and asset attachment, are documented. This investigation has not yet established whether any individual has been criminally convicted, or how much affected clients have been made whole.
